senses.definition: (of a story or statement) of doubtful authenticity, although widely circulated as being true
senses.example: The story about the inventor and the apple is probably apocryphal.

senses.definition: apt in the circumstances or in relation to something
senses.example: She ended her speech with an apposite quotation.

senses.definition: to take something for one's own use, typically without the owner's permission
senses.example: The general appropriated the villa as his headquarters.

senses.definition: to devote money or assets to a special purpose
senses.example: Congress appropriated funds for the new bridge.

words.note: As a verb, appropriate means to take for oneself, not just to be suitable.

senses.definition: a sign of what will happen; an omen
senses.example: The early lead was a good augury for the election.

senses.definition: threatening harm; menacing
senses.example: The guard dog gave us a baleful stare.

senses.definition: blissfully happy
senses.example: A beatific smile spread across the baby's face.

senses.definition: demonstrating aggression and willingness to fight
senses.example: The general's bellicose speeches alarmed neighboring states.

senses.definition: spiteful; bad-tempered
senses.example: The critic wrote a bilious review of the novel.

senses.definition: affected by nausea or vomiting
senses.example: The rough crossing left most passengers bilious.

senses.definition: a trite and unoriginal idea or remark, typically intended to soothe or placate
senses.example: The minister offered the usual bromides about patience.

senses.definition: self-assertive or proud to an irritating degree
senses.example: The bumptious intern corrected the director in front of everyone.

senses.definition: an absurd or comically exaggerated imitation of something, especially in a literary or dramatic work
senses.example: The play is a burlesque of grand opera.

senses.definition: to cause to appear absurd by parody
senses.example: The sketch burlesques the manners of the old aristocracy.

senses.definition: excessively complicated and typically involving a great deal of administrative detail
senses.example: Getting a permit meant navigating byzantine rules.

senses.definition: cautiously or suspiciously reluctant to do something
senses.example: Investors are chary of new tech start-ups.

senses.definition: exaggerated or aggressive patriotism
senses.example: Wartime chauvinism made any criticism look like treason.

senses.definition: excessive or prejudiced support for one's own group, especially prejudice against women
senses.example: She called out the chauvinism of the hiring panel.

senses.definition: a thing that is hoped or wished for but in fact is illusory or impossible to achieve
senses.example: A perfectly fair tax system may be a chimera.

senses.definition: stubbornly or willfully disobedient to authority
senses.example: The contumacious witness refused to answer the court's questions.

senses.definition: the final part of a play, film or narrative in which the strands of the plot are drawn together and matters are explained or resolved
senses.example: The novel's denouement reveals the true identity of the narrator.

senses.definition: lax in morals; licentious
senses.example: He spent a dissolute youth in the gambling houses of the city.

senses.definition: worthy of great respect
senses.example: The estimable judge served the court for forty years.

senses.definition: a person who is passionate about a particular cause, typically inciting change and taking radical action
senses.example: The young firebrand urged the workers to strike.

senses.definition: to become tired, weaker or less enthusiastic
senses.example: Interest in the project began to flag after the first year.

senses.definition: to mark an item for attention
senses.example: The software flags any unusual transactions.

words.note: As a verb, flag often means to grow tired or weak.

senses.definition: to limit or qualify something by conditions or exceptions
senses.example: She hedged her answer with several caveats.

senses.definition: to protect oneself against loss by supporting more than one possible result
senses.example: He hedged his bets by applying to five schools.

senses.definition: not conforming with accepted or orthodox standards or beliefs
senses.example: Her heterodox views on economics made her unpopular with colleagues.

senses.definition: to dispute the truth, validity or honesty of a statement or motive; to call into question
senses.example: The lawyer impugned the witness's credibility.

senses.definition: to represent something, especially something bad, as being done, caused or possessed by someone; to attribute
senses.example: They imputed the failure to poor leadership.

senses.definition: unable to be resisted or avoided; inescapable
senses.example: The novel builds to an ineluctable tragedy.

senses.definition: immoral or grossly unfair behavior
senses.example: The preacher railed against the iniquity of the city.

senses.definition: extreme patriotism, especially in the form of aggressive or warlike foreign policy
senses.example: The newspapers stoked jingoism before the war.

senses.definition: to act in an excessively subservient manner
senses.example: He refused to kowtow to the new owners.

senses.definition: looking or sounding sad and dismal
senses.example: The bloodhound has a lugubrious face.

senses.definition: ineffective or bungling; clumsy
senses.example: The maladroit waiter spilled soup on the guest.

senses.definition: a beggar
senses.example: Mendicants lined the steps of the temple.

senses.definition: given to begging
senses.example: The friars belonged to a mendicant order.

senses.definition: (of a fact or circumstance) to be a powerful or conclusive factor in preventing
senses.example: His youth militated against his promotion.

words.note: Militate means to weigh against something; mitigate means to lessen.

senses.definition: expressing or conveying a threat
senses.example: The letter had a minatory tone.

senses.definition: a person who has done something wrong or unlawful
senses.example: Police are searching for the miscreants who vandalized the park.

senses.definition: to make a disease or its symptoms less severe without removing the cause
senses.example: The drugs palliate the pain but do not cure the illness.

senses.definition: to disguise the seriousness of an offense
senses.example: Nothing can palliate such cruelty.

senses.definition: relating to or consisting of money
senses.example: He had no pecuniary interest in the deal.

senses.definition: to attack or ridicule publicly
senses.example: The minister was pilloried in the press.

senses.definition: (of a person or animal) not easily upset or excited
senses.example: The placid cow didn't even look up.

senses.definition: to talk at length in a foolish or inconsequential way
senses.example: He prattled on about his golf game for an hour.

senses.definition: foolish or inconsequential talk
senses.example: She was tired of his prattle.

senses.definition: showing a lack of courage or determination; timid
senses.example: The pusillanimous council refused to take a stand.

senses.definition: aggressively greedy or grasping
senses.example: The rapacious landlord raised the rent every year.

senses.definition: shining very brightly
senses.example: The refulgent sunset lit the whole sky.

senses.definition: an unprincipled person
senses.example: The old reprobate gambled away his family's savings.

senses.definition: unprincipled
senses.example: His reprobate friends led him into trouble.

senses.definition: extravagantly or excessively ornate, especially in music or literature
senses.example: The writer's rococo style is hard to read.

senses.definition: a position requiring little or no work but giving the holder status or financial benefit
senses.example: The post of honorary advisor was a sinecure.

senses.definition: bad-tempered; spiteful
senses.example: The columnist wrote splenetic attacks on modern art.

senses.definition: to speak badly of or tell lies about someone so as to damage their reputation
senses.example: The campaign traduced her record as governor.

senses.definition: unaccustomed or unusual
senses.example: She spoke with unwonted sharpness.

senses.definition: excessively proud of oneself or one's achievements
senses.example: The vainglorious general boasted of victories he never won.
